records.label: Patient #1
quotes: Patient #1 of the German family 13-501 carries a heterozygous c.713T > C nucleotide change in exon 7 of the IMPG1 gene that leads to a p.(Leu238Pro) amino acid substitution
The fundus of both eyes revealed central RPE abnormalities with foveal detachment (images not available). Patient #1 is the only affected member in the family.

records.label: Patient #2

phenotypes.text: bilateral singular central vitelliform macular lesion
dome-shaped foveal detachment of neurosensory retina
borderline to slightly reduced EOG Arden ratio

records.segregation: Both parents heterozygous and clinically unaffected
quotes: A second IMPG1 mutation, c.807 + 5G > A, was found in patient #2 of the consanguineous Turkish family 11-151 in a homozygous state (Table 1). Homozygosity was confirmed by segregation analysis in the genomic DNA of the parents.

Patient #2 was initially diagnosed with vitelliform macular dystrophy at the age of 2 (Table 2). During an eight year follow-up period the boy demonstrated fluctuating visual acuity of ~0.2 logMAR in both eyes. Electrophysiology at the age of 10 revealed normal findings in mfERG and a borderline to slightly abnormally low Arden Ratio in EOG measurements
Color fundus images showed a singular, vitelliform lesion in the central macula of both eyes, but otherwise normal fundus features (Figure 2A).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal foveal morphology on macular OCT

phenotypes.text: slightly decreased central retinal sensitivity on multifocal ERG, left eye

quotes: We describe a case of a 25-year-old female patient with symptomatic scotoma and vision decrease who exhibited bilateral small foveal yellow spots.
Optical coherence tomography revealed disorganization and decreased reflectance of the foveal ellipsoid and interdigitation zones in the left eye more than in the right eye.
Genetic testing identified a heterozygous p.Leu154Pro mutation in the IMPG1 gene.

records.label: Index autosomal dominant RP family
quotes: Exome sequencing was carried out for identifying the disease-causing gene in a family with autosomal dominant RP.
Exome sequencing of a family with RP revealed a splice variant in IMPG1.

records.label: Two families with the same IMPG1 splice variant (RP or VMD)
quotes: Subsequently, the same variant was identified in individuals from two families with either RP or VMD.

records.label: Eight additional families with IMPG1 missense or nonsense variants

variants.as_reported: different missense or nonsense variants in IMPG1

quotes: A retrospective study of patients with RP or VMD revealed eight additional families with different missense or nonsense variants in IMPG1.

notes.statement: Olivier et al. (2021) used morpholinos to knock down Impg1 and its paralog Impg2 in medaka fish. The resulting phenotype matched that seen in the families and included shorter rod and cone photoreceptor outer segments.
quotes: Using morpholino-mediated ablation of Impg1 and its paralog Impg2 in medaka fish, we confirmed a phenotype consistent with that observed in the families, including a decreased length of rod and cone photoreceptor outer segments.

notes.statement: Olivier et al. (2021) revised the clinical diagnosis for an IMPG1 retinopathy-associated variant. It had first been described as benign concentric annular macular dystrophy and was reclassified as retinitis pigmentosa with early macular involvement.
quotes: the clinical diagnosis of the IMPG1 retinopathy-associated variant, originally described as benign concentric annular macular dystrophy, was also revised to RP with early macular involvement.

notes.statement: Olivier et al. (2021) screened 596 families with retinitis pigmentosa or vitelliform macular dystrophy by gene panel testing and exome sequencing. They concluded that monoallelic or biallelic IMPG1 variants are associated with RP, similar to what has been reported for IMPG2.
quotes: Gene panel testing and exome sequencing were performed in 596 RP and VMD families to identified additional IMPG1 variants.
This study discusses a previously unreported association between monoallelic or biallelic IMPG1 variants and RP. Notably, similar observations have been reported for IMPG2.

notes.statement: Gupta et al. (2021) suggested that the IMPG1 p.Leu154Pro mutation, which has been implicated in adult-onset foveomacular vitelliform dystrophy, may cause symptomatic outer retinal disturbance in the heterozygous state. They noted that further studies were needed.
quotes: The p.Leu154Pro IMPG1 mutation may cause symptomatic outer retinal disturbance in the heterozygous state. Further studies are necessary.

notes.statement: Brandl et al. (2017) screened IMPG1 and IMPG2 in 106 VMD patients who had tested negative for BEST1 and PRPH2 mutations. They found IMPG1 mutations in 2 simplex cases with onset in early childhood: a heterozygous p.Leu238Pro missense mutation and a homozygous c.807+5G-A splice site mutation.
quotes: We therefore performed a mutational screen in a cohort of 106 BEST1/PRPH2-negative VMD patients in two genes encoding secreted interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycans-1 and -2 (IMPG1 and IMPG2).

We identified two novel mutations in IMPG1 in two simplex VMD cases with disease onset in their early childhood, a heterozygous p.(Leu238Pro) missense mutation and a homozygous c.807 + 5G > A splice site mutation.

notes.statement: In a minigene assay in HEK293 cells, Brandl et al. (2017) found that the IMPG1 c.807+5G-A mutation caused skipping of exon 7 in about half of the transcripts. They suggested that the aberrant mRNA likely undergoes nonsense-mediated decay.
quotes: exon 7 was skipped in about half of the transcripts leading to a 194 bp as well as the 335 bp reverse transcription (RT)-PCR product amplified in controls (Figure 1).
The in vitro splice assay thus confirms the bioinformatic prediction of missplicing due to the c.807 + 5G > A variant that likely leads to nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) of the aberrant mRNA.

notes.statement: Brandl et al. (2017) found that the heterozygous parents of the patient homozygous for c.807+5G-A were asymptomatic, with normal retinal imaging. They suggested that the correctly spliced transcripts provide enough functional IMPG1 to prevent even subclinical abnormalities in heterozygous carriers.
quotes: Our finding that a significant fraction of pre-mRNAs harboring the c.807 + 5G > A mutation are correctly spliced suggests that the level of functional IMPG1 is sufficient to prevent even subclinical abnormalities in heterozygous carriers.

notes.statement: Brandl et al. (2017) noted that p.Leu238Pro was the second missense mutation affecting IMPG1 residue Leu238 in a VMD patient, after the previously reported p.Leu238Arg. They proposed that defective IMPG1 causes disease through an as yet unknown dominant-negative effect or haploinsufficiency.
quotes: Thus, the current finding of a second missense mutation affecting amino acid p.(Leu238) in a patient with VMD supports the causative role of defective IMPG1 molecules in disease via an as yet unknown dominant-negative effect or haploinsufficiency.

notes.statement: Brandl et al. (2017) described a common sequence of stages in patients with IMPG1 or IMPG2 mutations. First came singular central vitelliform lesions with the material lying above a preserved Bruch membrane/RPE; this material was then resorbed, leaving an optically empty cavity; finally there was central atrophy with RPE loss. Clinical symptoms tended to be more severe with IMPG1 mutations.
quotes: (i) singular vitelliform lesions in the central macula with detachment of the neurosensory retina in SD-OCT, with hyperreflective material located above the seemingly preserved Bruch’s membrane/RPE; (ii) resorption of the hyperreflective material leaving behind a dome-shaped, optically empty cavity
Clinical symptoms tend to be more severe for IMPG1 mutations.

notes.statement: In the same cohort, Brandl et al. (2017) also found heterozygous IMPG2 mutations (3 stop and 5 missense) in 8 VMD patients. The patients were symptomatic, with a mean age at diagnosis of 53.1 years.
quotes: Eight patients were found to carry heterozygous mutations in the IMPG2 gene including three stop mutations [p.(Glu226*), p.(Ser522*) and p.(Gln856*)] and five missense mutations
Mean age at initial diagnosis was 53.1 years (range 33–64 years, Table 2)

notes.statement: Meunier et al. (2014) found that patients with IMPG1 or IMPG2 mutations had late onset (mean 42 years) and moderate visual impairment (mean visual acuity 20/40). Drusen-like lesions adjacent to vitelliform deposits were seen in 9 of 13 patients, and electrooculogram results were normal or borderline in 9 cases.
quotes: Patients with IMPG1 or IMPG2 mutations had a late onset and moderate visual impairment (mean visual acuity, 20/40; mean age of onset, 42 years)
Drusen-like lesions adjacent to the vitelliform deposits were observed in 9 of 13 patients.
Electro-oculogram results were normal or borderline in 9 cases.

notes.statement: On SD-OCT, Meunier et al. (2014) observed that the vitelliform material lay above the retinal pigment epithelium at all stages, with the RPE well preserved and of normal reflectivity, located between ellipsoid and interdigitation lines; these features are not seen in classical BEST1 or PRPH2 vitelliform dystrophies.
quotes: The vitelliform material was above the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) at any stage of the macular dystrophy, and this epithelium was well preserved and maintained its classical reflectivity on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT).
These clinical characteristics are not observed in the classical forms of BEST1 or PRPH2 vitelliform dystrophies.

notes.statement: Meunier et al. (2014) screened 49 families with vitelliform macular dystrophy negative for BEST1 and PRPH2 mutations and found IMPG1 or IMPG2 to be causal in 8% (4 families: 3 IMPG1, 1 IMPG2).
quotes: Forty-nine families were included.
IMPG1 and IMPG2 are new causal genes in 8% of families negative for BEST1 and PRPH2 mutations.

notes.statement: Meunier et al. (2014) recommended screening IMPG1 and IMPG2 in adult-onset vitelliform dystrophy with moderate visual impairment, drusen-like lesions, normal RPE reflectivity on SD-OCT, and vitelliform deposits between the ellipsoid and interdigitation lines.
quotes: These genes should be screened in adult-onset vitelliform dystrophy with (1) moderate visual impairment, (2) drusen-like lesions, (3) normal reflectivity of the RPE line on SD-OCT, and (4) vitelliform deposits located between ellipsoid and interdigitation lines on SD-OCT.

notes.statement: Manes et al. (2013) described vitelliform macular dystrophies as inherited retinal dystrophies marked by yellow, round deposits seen on fundus examination. These deposits occur in juvenile Best macular dystrophy and in adult-onset vitelliform macular dystrophy. For many affected individuals the genetic cause was unknown.
quotes: Vitelliform macular dystrophies (VMD) are inherited retinal dystrophies characterized by yellow, round deposits visible upon fundus examination and encountered in individuals with juvenile Best macular dystrophy (BMD) or adult-onset vitelliform macular dystrophy (AVMD).

notes.statement: Manes et al. (2013) screened 144 probands with various forms of macular dystrophy and found 3 further IMPG1 mutations in 2 families with autosomal recessive VMD. They concluded that IMPG1 mutations cause both autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive VMD, suggesting that impairment of the interphotoreceptor matrix might be a general cause of VMD.
quotes: Screening of 144 probands who had various forms of macular dystrophy revealed three other IMPG1 mutations.
We conclude that IMPG1 mutations cause both autosomal-dominant and -recessive forms of VMD, thus indicating that impairment of the interphotoreceptor matrix might be a general cause of VMD.

notes.statement: Manes et al. (2013) noted that IMPG1 encodes SPACR, a component of the rod and cone photoreceptor extracellular matrix domains. Structural modeling indicated that the p.Leu238Arg substitution destabilizes the conserved SEA1 domain of SPACR.
quotes: IMPG1 encodes the SPACR protein, a component of the rod and cone photoreceptor extracellular matrix domains. Structural modeling indicates that the p.Leu238Arg substitution destabilizes the conserved SEA1 domain of SPACR.

notes.statement: Manes et al. (2013) found that most patients with IMPG1 mutations had a normal or moderately decreased electrooculogram Arden ratio.
quotes: Most cases had a normal or moderately decreased electrooculogram Arden ratio.
